item.title: Taiji: Whale Watching and Whaling Heritage — Guide
item.description: Taiji, a small harbour town on Wakayama’s southeast coast, has one of the most complicated relationships with whales of anywhere in Japan: organised whaling began here in the early 1600s and shaped the town’s entire identity, while today it also runs whale- and dolphin-watching boats into the rich Kumano-nada waters offshore. The Taiji Whale Museum documents this long history with skeletons, historic whaling equipment and displays on the town’s traditions, and also keeps live cetaceans.
